timeline.current_model: AGO2 is the catalytic core of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC), performing endonucleolytic cleavage of target mRNAs guided by loaded small RNAs (miRNAs/siRNAs); its activity is regulated by multiple post-translational modifications (phosphorylation at S387 by MEK, acetylation by p300/CBP/HDAC7, malonylation by cytoplasmic SIRT3), by chaperone-mediated loading (Hsp90/p23/FKBP4), and by autophagy-dependent degradation via NDP52; AGO2 subcellular localization (cytoplasm vs. nucleus vs. mitochondria) is dynamically controlled by the Pi3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and determines distinct functional outputs—cytoplasmic RISC-mediated mRNA silencing, nuclear transcriptional regulation and transposon repression (via catalytic slicer activity), and mitochondrial translation activation via TUFM recruitment; AGO2 also engages KRAS at the ER, promotes telomerase activity through TERT-TERC association, facilitates homologous recombination by recruiting Rad51 to double-strand breaks, and participates in transcriptional activation via the RITA complex at promoters.
